summary: Corrado Pensa worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, having studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).

Craig J. Reynolds is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College (~1959–1963) and Cornell University (~1964–1973), and held posts at the Australian National University around 1989.

Craig Jamieson is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Affiliated with the University of Cambridge, he was attested there in 2002, and in 2012 served as curator for its South Asia manuscript collection and as a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge.
Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed studies at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981).

Cristina Pecchia is an Indologist and Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (PhD ~1999–2003) and the University of Vienna (2000), and worked as a project researcher at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2009).

Csaba Dezső specializes in Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1992–1999) and earned a PhD at the University of Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. Around 2002, he became an Assistant Lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.

Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (2003–2009). He has held posts as a research assistant at Eötvös Loránd University and at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held an appointment as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Toronto (attested 2017) and held a post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018).
Culadasa was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied under Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu. He served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011).
Cuma Ozkan is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).

Cuong T. Mai works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii and a PhD at Indiana University under John R. McRae (attested 2009), later serving as Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Keizaburō Mizuno and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).
Cynthia Col is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark C. Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool (~1930–1934) and SOAS University of London (~1934–1936). He served as Director of SOAS (~1956–1976) and held a post at the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Washington (-1996) under Leonard van der Kuijp. He has served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein (-2017) and later served there as a research fellow.

D. C. Lau was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1939–1946) and held posts at SOAS University of London (~1950–1978) and University College London (1970–1978).
D. C. Sarasvati was an Indologist who studied under V. Raghavan (attested 1978). She served as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.

D. Dennis Hudson was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He taught in the Department of Religion and served as Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College (~1970–2004).

D. Neil Schmid is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, and also studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Waseda University.
